key_insight: You can extract reliable Q-value estimates from a behavior-cloned policy and use them to gate online RL updates, allowing robots to improve through on-robot reinforcement learning without overwriting demonstrated good actions.
problem_solved: Behavior Cloning (BC) provides strong initial policies but lacks a safe, self-guided mechanism for online improvement; existing offline-to-online methods often degrade performance by replacing good demonstrated actions due to distribution mismatch.
method: Q-Estimation: derive Q-value estimates from the behavior-cloned policy and demonstration data to assess action quality.
Q-Gating: use the estimated Q-values to selectively allow online RL updates only where expected improvement exists, preventing replacement of high-quality demonstrated actions.
On-robot integration: run a lightweight RL loop on the robot that uses the Q-gates to make sample-efficient, safe policy refinements in real time.
impact: Enables safe, sample-efficient offline-to-online robot learning that preserves demonstrated behavior while allowing targeted improvement, lowering the risk of catastrophic degradation during on-robot RL and accelerating real-world deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Demonstrations → Behavior Cloning → Q-Estimator → Q-Gating → On-robot RL loop
Before/After performance chart: BC baseline vs BC+Q2RL showing preserved performance and improved returns over online learning steps
Policy overlay: state visualization highlighting actions gated (preserved) vs actions allowed to change
Iconography: robot + shield (safety/preservation), upward arrow (improvement), clock (sample efficiency)
paper_title: When Life Gives You BC, Make Q-functions: Extracting Q-values from Behavior Cloning for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Lakshita Dodeja, Ondrej Biza, Shivam Vats, Stephen Hart, Stefanie Tellex
